answer: Residual Attention Curve. Each new identity draws a limited attention allotment from a shared per-epoch budget; once the local vertex of demand is reached, issuance cost rises sharply with each additional identity from the same source. An attacker must either pay escalating issuance costs or spread across many epochs, paying a meadow of idle waiting time. Residual pigment from prior activity decays, so recycled identities lose standing and cost more to revive.
